key_insight: Multimodal wearable models predicted perceived exertion better than pulse-rate-only models in frail patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD).
clinical_relevance: The findings may inform exertion monitoring during ESKD prehabilitation; this study does not address cancer or drug discovery.
method: Collected smartwatch pulse rate, electrodermal activity, skin temperature, and accelerometer data during prehabilitation.
Built individualized machine-learning models to predict Rating of Perceived Exertion.
Compared pulse-rate-only models with multi-feature models.
evidence_signal: Among 13 ESKD participants and 13 healthy older controls, multi-feature models significantly improved ESKD predictions, achieving a root mean square error of 1.33.
watch_item: The small cohort and individualized modeling warrant larger, independent validation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Wearable Sensors Predict Exertion Without Changes in Pulse Rate for Frail End-Stage Kidney Disease Patients
